mainProgression.description: Classic 12-bar blues progression using the three primary chords of the key. The foundation of rock and roll guitar.

sectionProgressions.progression: A - A - A - A - D - D - A - A - E - D - A - E
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: I - I - I - I - IV - IV - I - I - V - IV - I - V
sectionProgressions.description: Standard 12-bar blues form with a quick-change variation. Each chord lasts one bar at the brisk 176 BPM tempo.
The final two bars of each 12-bar cycle create a turnaround that drives back to the top of the form.

harmonicFunction: A (I) - Tonic chord providing the home base and dominant feel of the song
D (IV) - Subdominant chord creating movement away from tonic in bars 5-6
E (V) - Dominant chord creating tension and resolution back to the tonic

techniques.name: 12-Bar Blues Rhythm
techniques.description: The fundamental 12-bar blues shuffle rhythm pattern that underpins all of rock and roll, played with a driving downstroke feel at a fast tempo

notes: A: X-0-2-2-2-0 (open A major chord)
D: X-X-0-2-3-2 (open D major chord)
E: 0-2-2-1-0-0 (open E major chord)
Can also be played as A7, D7, E7 for authentic blues color
The shuffle feel gives each beat a triplet swing: long-short, long-short
sequence: Learn the three open chord shapes: A, D, and E
Practice the 12-bar form: 4 bars A, 2 bars D, 2 bars A, 1 bar E, 1 bar D, 2 bars A
Add the shuffle rhythm feel with accented downstrokes
Build up to the fast 176 BPM tempo gradually
tips: Start at half tempo (88 BPM) and work up gradually
Focus on strong downstrokes with a percussive attack
Keep your strumming hand loose to maintain the fast tempo without fatigue
Count the 12 bars carefully until the form becomes second nature
details.progression: A - A - A - A - D - D - A - A - E - D - A - E

techniques.name: Shuffle Strumming
techniques.description: A swung eighth-note strumming pattern that gives the song its driving rock and roll groove, emphasizing beats 2 and 4 for the classic backbeat

notes: The shuffle feel swings the eighth notes into a triplet-based rhythm
Accent beats 2 and 4 for the classic backbeat feel
Use all downstrokes for maximum power at high tempo
Palm muting can be added lightly on the lower strings for tighter sound
sequence: Practice the shuffle rhythm on muted strings first
Add the A chord and strum the shuffle pattern for 4 bars
Practice transitioning to D at bar 5 without losing the groove
Work through the full 12-bar form maintaining the shuffle feel
tips: Listen to the original recording to internalize the shuffle feel
Tap your foot on beats 1 and 3 while accenting strums on 2 and 4
Keep your wrist relaxed - tension will slow you down at this tempo
The groove matters more than perfect chord voicings
details.progression: Shuffle rhythm applied to all chord changes

sections.name: Intro
sections.description: Brief guitar and band intro establishing the fast shuffle groove in A
notes: Band kicks in together with a driving shuffle rhythm
Establish the tempo immediately - this song is fast at 176 BPM
Strong downstrokes on the A chord set the energy level

sections.name: Verse (12-Bar Blues)
sections.description: The main verse follows a standard 12-bar blues form with the iconic 'You ainthe signature lyric
sections.progression: A - A - A - A - D - D - A - A - E - D - A - E
notes: Standard 12-bar blues form repeated for each verse
Maintain steady shuffle rhythm throughout all 12 bars
The chord changes follow the words naturally
Keep the energy high and the tempo driving

sections.name: Guitar Solo
sections.description: Scotty Moore's guitar solo over the 12-bar blues form, using blues scale licks and double stops
sections.progression: A - A - A - A - D - D - A - A - E - D - A - E
notes: For beginners, continue strumming the 12-bar blues rhythm during the solo section
The solo follows the same 12-bar chord structure
Advanced players can learn Scotty Moore's blues-influenced solo licks
The rhythm guitar maintains the shuffle pattern underneath

sections.name: Final Verse / Outro
sections.description: Repeated verses building energy to the final ending with a classic rock and roll stop-time finish
sections.progression: A - A - A - A - D - D - A - A - E - D - A - A
notes: Final verses repeat the same 12-bar form with increasing intensity
The ending resolves firmly on the A chord (tonic)
Band stops together on the final hit
Keep the shuffle groove locked in right to the end

guitar.recommended: Gibson ES-295 or any semi-hollow electric guitar
alternatives: Any acoustic guitar with steel strings
Any guitar with a warm, clean tone
guitar.pickup: Neck pickup or P-90 style for warm, round tone

effects.distortion: None - clean to mild tube breakup
effects.delay: Light slapback echo (80-120ms) for authentic 1950s Sun Studio sound
effects.reverb: Light spring reverb for vintage ambiance
effects.other: No effects pedals needed. The raw, clean guitar tone is essential to the sound.

beginner.focus: Learn the three open chords and the 12-bar blues form
steps: Learn open A, D, and E chord shapes individually
Practice switching between A and D, then D and E, then A and E
Memorize the 12-bar blues form: 4 bars A, 2 bars D, 2 bars A, 1 bar E, 1 bar D, 2 bars A
Strum quarter notes at a slow tempo through the entire form

intermediate.focus: Add the shuffle rhythm and build up to performance tempo
steps: Learn the shuffle strumming pattern with swung eighth notes
Practice the shuffle feel on each chord individually
Play through the full 12-bar form with shuffle rhythm at 120 BPM
Gradually increase tempo toward 176 BPM over several practice sessions

advanced.focus: Master the full tempo with authentic feel and optional soloing
steps: Play the complete song at 176 BPM with tight, driving shuffle rhythm
Add dynamics and vocal accompaniment while strumming
Learn basic blues scale licks in A for the solo section
Experiment with dominant 7th chord voicings (A7, D7, E7) for authentic blues color

commonMistakes: Losing count of the 12 bars - the form is the foundation, count carefully
Playing straight eighth notes instead of shuffle feel - listen to the swing
Tensing up the strumming hand at fast tempo - stay relaxed
Missing the chord change to D at bar 5 - anticipate the change
practiceRoutine: Warm up with A, D, E chord changes for 3 minutes
Practice the shuffle strum on muted strings for 2 minutes to build the groove
Play through one 12-bar cycle slowly, counting each bar out loud
Gradually increase tempo by 10 BPM increments each pass
Run through the complete song structure at target tempo
focusAreas: Quick chord transitions at fast tempo
metronomeWork: Start at 100 BPM with the shuffle pattern on a single chord
Increase by 10 BPM increments as comfort builds
Practice at 140 BPM with full chord changes before pushing to 176 BPM
Set the metronome to click on beats 2 and 4 for authentic backbeat feel
